target.transport: native USB composite CDC and HID mouse
target.current_device_policy: Do not flash or alter the StickS3 currently in use; all device tests wait for the fresh unit.

validated_facts.fact: The internal IMU is a BMI270 at I2C address 0x68 on SDA GPIO47 and SCL GPIO48.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack StickS3 documentation and M5Unified StickS3 board implementation

validated_facts.fact: The internal infrared transmitter is GPIO46 and the infrared receiver is GPIO42.
The infrared receiver is a demodulating digital receiver intended for RMT pulse capture, not an analog reflectance channel.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack documents RMT-only reception and its remote-control distance guidance; this makes blink sensing unproven until measured.

validated_facts.fact: The internal IR path needs the controlled external 5 V output and must not be enabled while an external source drives that rail.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack StickS3 power and IR documentation; firmware defaults the rail off and requires a physical two-second hold.

validated_facts.fact: USB HID on ESP32-S3 requires TinyUSB native mode ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0; ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 selects hardware USB-JTAG CDC and cannot run USBHIDMouse.
validated_facts.validation: Espressif Arduino core 2.0.17 and 3.x USB examples, installed core sources, and Context7 official-source excerpts

validated_facts.fact: Wokwi can execute a generic ESP32-S3 DevKitC firmware image, but its documented board list does not provide a complete StickS3 model.
validated_facts.validation: Official Wokwi ESP32 guide, Wokwi CLI documentation, Context7 Wokwi documentation index, and a successful Wokwi CLI run of the cross-compiled simulator harness

tasks.name: Separate StickS3 target
acceptance: Legacy AVR source remains untouched.
StickS3 has its own pinned PlatformIO environment.
A native host-test environment compiles sensor-independent logic.

tasks.name: Safe USB head-mouse prototype
acceptance: BMI270 data calibrates only while stationary.
Movement uses gyro rate with filtering, deadzone, fractional accumulation, and bounded HID reports.
The device emits no pointer movement until mouse mode is physically armed for two seconds.
Axis directions are verified and adjusted on the glasses mount before user testing.

tasks.name: Onboard IR blink feasibility probe
acceptance: Transmit GPIO46 emits a controlled 38 kHz carrier envelope through RMT.
Receive GPIO42 captures raw demodulated pulse timing through RMT.
CDC logs retain timestamp, validity, symbol count, active time, total time, normalized ratio, and protocol stage.
The guided test measures open eye, closed eye, and repeated blinks without assuming signal polarity.
A pass requires at least 20 valid frames in each baseline, at least 4 sigma separation, at least 15 percent relative change, and at least two human-duration blink events.

tasks.name: External click-sensor boundary
acceptance: Blink classification consumes a sensor-neutral normalized sample.
A future analog TCRT5000 implementation can replace the onboard IR producer without changing USB click behavior.
No TCRT5000 purchase is recommended before the onboard test gate is evaluated.

tasks.name: Fresh-device bench validation
acceptance: Firmware build completes without flashing as the pre-hardware gate.
Fresh StickS3 enumerates as both CDC and HID without spontaneous mouse reports.
Display reports BMI270 and stationary calibration succeeds.
IR test is repeated at the intended eye distance and geometry in at least two ambient-light conditions.
Five deliberate blinks are attempted per run and raw CSV is retained.

tasks.name: Generic ESP32-S3 simulator gate
acceptance: The portable production motion and blink-analysis sources cross-compile for a generic ESP32-S3 target.
Wokwi CLI lints the diagram and boots the firmware image.

The simulated firmware validates stationary gyro calibration, moving-calibration rejection, cursor deadzone, pointer direction and accumulation, invalid timestep rejection, optical separation, blink timing and refractory behavior, and the complete guided feasibility protocol.
The run emits COLIBRINO_SIM_PASS and does not claim to validate unmodeled StickS3 peripherals or optics.

simulation_boundary.validated_in_wokwi: ESP32-S3 compilation and execution of sensor-independent motion, statistics, blink detection, and feasibility state-machine logic.
simulation_boundary.requires_sticks3_hardware: BMI270 initialization and axis orientation, M5PM1 power control, display, buttons, internal IR electrical and optical behavior, composite TinyUSB CDC/HID enumeration, and end-to-end cursor/click behavior.

sensor_purchase_decision.onboard_ir_pass: Keep the integrated IR path only if two repeat runs pass and at least four of five deliberate blinks are detected in each run with no false click during a 30-second open-eye control.
sensor_purchase_decision.inconclusive_retest: Reposition and repeat when valid frames are below 80 percent or geometry changed during capture.
sensor_purchase_decision.external_sensor_required: Use an external analog reflectance sensor such as TCRT5000 when open/closed separation remains below the gate, deliberate-blink recall is below four of five after positioning trials, or false clicks appear in the open-eye control.

remaining_hardware_questions: Which StickS3 gyro axes and signs correspond to horizontal and vertical cursor motion in the final glasses mount?
Does the fixed physical spacing and optical orientation of the integrated IR pair return enough modulated reflection from an eyelid at the intended distance?
Does direct transmitter-to-receiver optical coupling saturate the digital receiver and erase the open-versus-closed difference?
What mounting position provides repeatable blink sensing without putting the StickS3 body in the user's field of view?
